import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Integrals.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
Verification status: uncompiled candidate. See `docs/part2/HANDOFF.md`.

# Genuine integrals for the adopted paired positive fibre

The local certificate has coordinates `(t, u, z, w)` with
`tl < t < tr`, `ul < u < ur`, and `a < w < z < Z`.
Its integrand is `K / (80 * t * u * z^2 * w)`.

This file defines the literal iterated Lebesgue integral and evaluates it
using the fundamental theorem of calculus. The definitions contain no
stored certificate bounds. Endpoints are finite interval endpoints; for
Lebesgue measure, changing a finite set of one-dimensional endpoints does
not change these integrals.

The equality proved here does not assert that the local fibre has passed
the manuscript's region and mask checks, or that a family of such fibres
has been combined with its error ledger. Those are separate obligations.
-/

namespace ImbalancedChen.Certificates

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped Interval

/-- The remaining genuine one-dimensional fibre integral after integrating
`1 / w` over the actual interval from `a` to `z`. -/
def pairedFibreIntegral (a Z : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ z in a..Z, Real.log (z / a) / z ^ 2

private theorem hasDerivAt_pairedFibrePrimitive {a z : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hz : 0 < z) :
    HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => -((1 + Real.log x - Real.log a) / x))
      (Real.log (z / a) / z ^ 2) z := by
  have hd := (((hasDerivAt_const z (1 : ℝ)).add
    (Real.hasDerivAt_log hz.ne')).sub_const (Real.log a)).div
      (hasDerivAt_id z) hz.ne'
  apply hd.neg.congr_deriv
  dsimp
  rw [Real.log_div hz.ne' ha.ne']
  field_simp [hz.ne']
  ring

/-- The fibre kernel is integrable on the complete closed interval.
Its logarithm and denominator stay within their actual domains. -/
theorem intervalIntegrable_pairedFibreKernel {a Z : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hAZ : a ≤ Z) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun z : ℝ => Real.log (z / a) / z ^ 2)
      volume a Z := by
  have hzpos : ∀ z ∈ Set.uIcc a Z, 0 < z := by
    intro z hz
    rw [Set.uIcc_of_le hAZ] at hz
    exact ha.trans_le hz.1
  apply ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable
  refine ((continuousOn_id.div_const a).log ?_).div (continuousOn_id.pow 2) ?_
  · intro z hz
    exact (div_pos (hzpos z hz) ha).ne'
  · intro z hz
    exact pow_ne_zero 2 (hzpos z hz).ne'

/-- Exact analytic evaluation of the positive triangular fibre.
The hypotheses allow the degenerate endpoint `a = Z`, when both sides
are zero. -/
theorem pairedFibreIntegral_eq {a Z : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hAZ : a ≤ Z) :
    pairedFibreIntegral a Z =
      1 / a - (1 + Real.log (Z / a)) / Z := by
  let F : ℝ → ℝ := fun z => -((1 + Real.log z - Real.log a) / z)
  have hzpos : ∀ z ∈ Set.uIcc a Z, 0 < z := by
    intro z hz
    rw [Set.uIcc_of_le hAZ] at hz
    exact ha.trans_le hz.1
  have hd : ∀ z ∈ Set.uIcc a Z,
      HasDerivAt F (Real.log (z / a) / z ^ 2) z := by
    intro z hz
    exact hasDerivAt_pairedFibrePrimitive ha (hzpos z hz)
  calc
    pairedFibreIntegral a Z = F Z - F a :=
      intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt hd
        (intervalIntegrable_pairedFibreKernel ha hAZ)
    _ = 1 / a - (1 + Real.log (Z / a)) / Z := by
      dsimp [F]
      rw [Real.log_div (ha.trans_le hAZ).ne' ha.ne']
      ring

/-- The actual rational kernel, written in factored form to expose Fubini
coordinates without introducing an external numerical approximation. -/
def pairedFibreKernel (t u z w : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (1 / t) * ((1 / u) * ((1 / z ^ 2) * (1 / w)))

theorem pairedFibreKernel_eq (t u z w : ℝ) :
    pairedFibreKernel t u z w = 1 / (t * u * z ^ 2 * w) := by
  simp [pairedFibreKernel, one_div, mul_inv_rev, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc]

/-- The complete local contribution is a genuine four-variable iterated
integral over `a < w < z < Z`, with the literal manuscript coefficient.
It is independent of any claimed stored lower or upper endpoint. -/
def pairedLocalIntegral (K a tl tr ul ur Z : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (K / 80) * ∫ t in tl..tr, ∫ u in ul..ur,
    ∫ z in a..Z, ∫ w in a..z, pairedFibreKernel t u z w

/-- No alternate model is hidden by the factored kernel notation. -/
theorem pairedLocalIntegral_eq_literal (K a tl tr ul ur Z : ℝ) :
    pairedLocalIntegral K a tl tr ul ur Z =
      (K / 80) * ∫ t in tl..tr, ∫ u in ul..ur,
        ∫ z in a..Z, ∫ w in a..z, 1 / (t * u * z ^ 2 * w) := by
  simp only [pairedLocalIntegral, pairedFibreKernel_eq]

/-- Integrating the actual inner `w` coordinate gives the logarithmic
fibre profile. -/
theorem pairedFibreIntegral_eq_iterated {a Z : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hAZ : a ≤ Z) :
    (∫ z in a..Z, (1 / z ^ 2) * (∫ w in a..z, 1 / w)) =
      pairedFibreIntegral a Z := by
  apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
  intro z hz
  rw [Set.uIcc_of_le hAZ] at hz
  dsimp only
  rw [integral_one_div_of_pos ha (ha.trans_le hz.1)]
  ring

/-- The exact logarithmic expression for the actual local integral.
All three logarithms arise from proved real integration identities. -/
theorem pairedLocalIntegral_eq (K : ℝ) {a tl tr ul ur Z : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hAZ : a ≤ Z)
    (htl : 0 < tl) (htr : 0 < tr) (hul : 0 < ul) (hur : 0 < ur) :
    pairedLocalIntegral K a tl tr ul ur Z =
      (K / 80) * Real.log (tr / tl) * Real.log (ur / ul) *
        (1 / a - (1 + Real.log (Z / a)) / Z) := by
  unfold pairedLocalIntegral pairedFibreKernel
  simp only [intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul, intervalIntegral.integral_mul_const]
  rw [integral_one_div_of_pos htl htr,
    integral_one_div_of_pos hul hur,
    pairedFibreIntegral_eq_iterated ha hAZ,
    pairedFibreIntegral_eq ha hAZ]
  ring

end

end ImbalancedChen.Certificates

declarations.name: pairedFibreIntegral
declarations.review: Literal volume interval integral of log(z/a)/z^2, not an endpoint output

declarations.name: hasDerivAt_pairedFibrePrimitive
declarations.review: Differentiate F(x)=-((1+log x-log a)/x). Quotient rule and negation yield -(z inverse*z-(1+log z-log a))/z^2 = log(z/a)/z^2. ha,hz provide the nonzero arguments for log_div and field_simp. No equality of functions is silently assumed: congr_deriv changes only derivative value.

declarations.name: intervalIntegrable_pairedFibreKernel
declarations.review: On uIcc a Z=Icc a Z, ha and hAZ yield z>=a>0. Thus z/a>0 and z^2!=0. ContinuousOn.log and division give continuity on the complete closed interval; ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable supplies volume integrability.

declarations.name: pairedFibreIntegral_eq
declarations.review: FTC has exactly its required derivative and integrable derivative hypotheses. F(Z)-F(a)=1/a-(1+log(Z/a))/Z follows by log_div and ring. Z>0 follows from ha.trans_le hAZ. At a=Z both sides are zero.

declarations.name: pairedFibreKernel_eq
declarations.review: Total-field inverse identities prove exact equality with 1/(t*u*z^2*w), without positivity assumptions and without replacing the model

declarations.name: pairedLocalIntegral
declarations.review: Literal nested volume interval integrals, fixed order t,u,z,w, triangular w in a..z and z in a..Z, times K/80 once

declarations.name: pairedLocalIntegral_eq_literal
declarations.review: Definition unfolding and pointwise kernel equality only. This written theorem keeps K/80 outside the integral; by linearity and elementary division algebra its intended positive-domain mathematical value is the iterated integral of K/(80*t*u*z^2*w). No extra wrapper theorem is needed.

declarations.name: pairedFibreIntegral_eq_iterated
declarations.review: integral_congr requires EqOn on uIcc a Z. hAZ converts it to Icc and ha.trans_le hz.1 proves z>0. integral_one_div_of_pos ha hz integrates w exactly to log(z/a); ring changes multiplication by reciprocal square to division.

declarations.name: pairedLocalIntegral_eq
declarations.review: simp only extracts constants in the existing nested order with integral_const_mul/integral_mul_const. Remaining scalar factors are integral(1/t), integral(1/u) and integral(z^-2*integral(1/w)). The first two use the actual positive-endpoint API, the third uses the previous iterated identity and FTC endpoint identity. ring only reassociates the resulting factors. No Fubini exchange or product-measure assertion is used.

domain_and_normalization.intended_strict_domain: 0<tl<tr, 0<ul<ur, 0<a<Z, a<w<z<Z. Every reciprocal denominator is nonzero and positive. If K>0, the pointwise manuscript integrand is positive.
domain_and_normalization.theorem_hypotheses: Exactly ha:0<a, hAZ:a<=Z, htl:0<tl, htr:0<tr, hul:0<ul, hur:0<ur, and arbitrary real K. No assumptions are added, removed or weakened in source.
domain_and_normalization.endpoint_order: The written local evaluation does not require tl<=tr or ul<=ur: positive reverse intervals are oriented Lebesgue interval integrals and log(right/left) has the matching sign. Thus the original strict domain is covered, with additional valid oriented cases. Checker.Valid supplies tl<=tr and ul<=ur and proves upper endpoints positive in its consumer.
domain_and_normalization.degenerate_cases: a=Z, tl=tr or ul=ur give zero through the integral and matching log/bracket factor; no strictly positive result is claimed for arbitrary K or degenerate endpoints.
domain_and_normalization.open_boundary: Mathlib interval notation is volume over Ioc for forward endpoints. Null singleton endpoints identify this with the stated strict open coordinate domain; the nonzero/continuous formulas also hold at all included endpoints, including z=a,w=a.
domain_and_normalization.actual_integrability: For each fixed positive t,u,z, w reciprocal is continuous on [a,z]; after integration the z profile is a scalar times log(z/a)/z^2, explicitly proved integrable. The resulting outer u and t profiles are scalar multiples of positive-interval reciprocals. This explains genuine integrability of the iterated construction; the module does not need to exchange integration order.
domain_and_normalization.coefficient: K/80 appears once in the definition and once in the exact evaluation. No second factor 4 or 20 occurs.
domain_and_normalization.stored_outputs: No lower/upper certificate fields, numerical approximations, adopted-mask substitutes or stored output definitions appear in this module.
domain_and_normalization.boundary: This is local analytic evaluation. It does not certify mask membership, row disjointness, arithmetic mean licensing or the final C; original adopted source, K, C, selectors and quantifiers remain unchanged.
